name: State-level compliance exposure
blurb: Errors and omissions and D&O exposure from state specific safety and audit requirements.

points.desc: Errors and omissions and D&O exposure from state specific safety and audit requirements.
points.name: State-level compliance exposure

points.desc: Working from Orrick's state law tracker, RAND identified 189 state AI laws with a distinct civil or criminal penalty, enacted between 2006 and June 2026. It counts 28 on automated decision making, 22 on AI in political advertising, 18 on user facing AI such as chatbot disclosure and self harm protocols, and 14 on AI in health care. RAND notes that a new disclosure law can produce both enforcement and securities claims across many insureds at the same time.
points.name: 189 enacted state AI laws carry a penalty

summary: Errors and omissions and D&O exposure from state specific safety and audit requirements.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: An absolute pollution exclusion in the commercial general liability policy would bar claims from state environmental safety audit failures involving chemical or fuel spills.
A professional services exclusion in the commercial general liability policy would eliminate coverage for errors and omissions arising from state compliance consulting or audit services.
A prior acts exclusion with a retroactive date after the insured's first state audit would leave all earlier compliance failures uncovered.
A regulatory fines and penalties exclusion would defeat coverage for state agency enforcement actions seeking monetary penalties.
A contractual liability exclusion that is not amended to cover state audit obligations in client contracts would bar indemnity claims from clients.
A cyber liability exclusion in the errors and omissions policy would remove coverage for state data security audit failures leading to privacy breach claims.
A sublimit for bodily injury or property damage arising from fire safety violations would cap coverage far below the potential loss from a data centre fire.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Amend the professional services exclusion in the commercial general liability policy to cover state compliance consulting and audit services performed by the insured.
Add a regulatory proceedings endorsement to the directors and officers policy to cover defence costs for state agency investigations into safety and audit failures.
Delete the prior acts exclusion and set the retroactive date to the inception of the insured's first state regulated operation to cover all historical compliance failures.
Add contractual liability coverage for state audit obligations in client contracts, including indemnity for fines and penalties where insurable by law.
Carve back the fines and penalties exclusion to cover civil penalties imposed by state safety agencies, subject to a sublimit and only where permitted by state law.
Add a state privacy law endorsement to the errors and omissions policy to cover claims arising from state data security audit requirements, including private rights of action.
Negotiate a sublimit for emergency response and crisis management costs incurred when a state agency orders an immediate shutdown or evacuation due to noncompliance.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Business interruption waiting periods for state mandated shutdowns are typically 24 to 72 hours, but this exposure is not covered under the liability program and must be addressed in the property policy.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage for state compliance failures is contingent on physical damage from a covered cause, so a pure regulatory shutdown without physical loss would require a separate contingent business interruption or regulatory action extension.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic data processing equipment coverage is typically written on a separate property schedule with limits equal to the full replacement cost of servers, cooling systems and power distribution units, because state safety audits often focus on these assets.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Property damage from a state mandated shutdown due to noncompliant safety audit is covered under a separate property policy, not this liability placement, with limits set by the replacement cost of the data centre and its equipment.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: The commercial general liability policy remains on an occurrence basis for bodily injury and property damage from premises safety, but it will not respond to pure financial loss from state audit failures, which sits under the claims made professional liability policy.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims made basis applies to the errors and omissions and directors and officers coverage because state compliance failures may be discovered years after the audit period and claims made triggers on the date the claim is first made against the insured.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess umbrella towers follow form over the primary commercial general liability and the claims made professional liability policies, with each layer attaching only after the underlying limits are exhausted by payment of covered claims, and typical layer heights are five to ten million dollars each depending on the insured's state footprint and client contract requirements.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Bodily injury or property damage claims from employees, visitors or contractors alleging unsafe conditions due to failure to meet state fire or life safety codes.
Errors and omissions claims from clients alleging the insured failed to perform state mandated safety audits or misrepresented compliance status.
Directors and officers claims from shareholders alleging the board failed to oversee state compliance, leading to regulatory fines or business interruption.
Regulatory enforcement actions by state agencies seeking penalties for noncompliance with safety and audit requirements.
Contractual liability claims from clients seeking indemnification for losses caused by the insured's state compliance failures.
Third party claims for data breach or privacy violations under state laws where state audit requirements include data security controls.
Claims from neighbouring property owners alleging nuisance or pollution from noncompliant state environmental safety requirements.

underwriter_wants_to_know: Which states the insured operates in and which state safety and audit requirements apply to each facility.
Whether the insured has a central compliance tracking system for state specific safety codes and audit deadlines.
The frequency and scope of state mandated safety audits and whether any past audits resulted in findings or fines.
How the insured allocates responsibility for state compliance between internal teams and third party contractors.
Whether client contracts require the insured to indemnify clients for state compliance failures.
The insured's history of regulatory enforcement actions or whistleblower complaints related to state safety requirements.
Whether the insured has purchased separate environmental or cyber liability policies that may overlap with state audit exposures.
